patients.summary: 55-year-old warehouse supervisor with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity, achalasia treated with pneumatic dilation, alcohol use disorder, a resolved folate deficiency anemia, a passed uric acid ureteral stone, and gout now on allopurinol through rheumatology. Joined the practice in 2019.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Caller: Darren Upton, DOB 07/10/1971. Asking about becoming a patient here. Says his old office keeps rotating him between whoever is free and he can never get a call back about refills. Coworker at the distribution center recommended us.
Explained membership, that insurance still covers labs/specialists/meds. He is fine with that.
Scheduled new patient visit 9/12 at 8:00. Records release form emailed to darren.upton@example.test for his prior primary care office. Asked him to bring his pill bottles.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

48 y/o man joining the practice. Supervises a shift at a distribution warehouse; no regular exercise. Wanted a doctor who answers the phone.

Diabetes: type 2, found about four years ago at his previous office on routine labs. Metformin 1000 mg BID since then, tolerating it, occasional loose stool in the first year that settled. Last A1c he remembers was "in the sixes." No eye exam in over a year. No numbness in the feet, no polyuria.
Statin: atorvastatin 20 mg daily, started by the old office for the diabetes. No muscle aches.
Gout: one attack in the right big toe a few years back, treated short-term at the prior office, no recurrence that he can recall, never on a daily gout pill.
Kidney stone: one, roughly six years ago, passed it at home after a rough couple of days. No procedure.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: none to medications.
Surgeries: none.
FH: father with type 2 DM and gout. Mother with high blood pressure. Paternal uncle drank heavily.
SH: never smoked. Alcohol "socially, a few on weekends." No drug use. Married. Day shift, sometimes stays late.

ROS: negative in detail, including no chest pain, dyspnea, dysuria, flank pain, joint swelling.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, BP normal today. Ht 180 cm, wt 103.8 kg, BMI about 32. Well-appearing, heavyset. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen protuberant, soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Feet: pulses 2+, monofilament intact bilaterally, no calluses or ulcers. No joint swelling or tophi. Skin clear.

Assessment/plan
1. Type 2 diabetes, on metformin. A1c, CMP, urine albumin/creatinine today. Eye exam referral to an optometrist. Continue metformin.
2. Lipids on atorvastatin 20. Lipid panel today.
3. Gout, remote single flare. No treatment needed now. Will check uric acid if he has symptoms.
4. History of kidney stone. Hydration discussed.
5. Weight: BMI 32. Talked briefly about activity; he'd rather tackle it later.
6. Prevention: Tdap given today. HCV and HIV screening today, he agreed. Colon cancer screening due at 45 under the newer guidance once he's eligible, will plan with him in the next year or two. Flu shot when it arrives.
7. Records requested from the prior office.

RTC 6 months for diabetes, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Darren, your labs from Thursday are back. A1c is in the low 6 range, which is good control for diabetes. Kidney and liver tests normal, no protein in the urine. Cholesterol is reasonable on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. No changes; keep doing what you're doing. We'll send a reminder when flu vaccine is in.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM, left deltoid. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. VIS given. Waited 15 minutes, no issues. Pt on his way to the 8 o'clock shift.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax after second request (first request 9/12, re-sent 10/15). 46 pages scanned to chart.

Summary for PCP review:
- Type 2 diabetes diagnosed 2015 on routine fasting labs; metformin started then and titrated to 1000 mg BID. A1c values 6.1 to 6.6 over 2016 to 2019.
- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily since 2016.
- Office note 2016: acute pain and swelling of the right great toe, treated as gout with a short course of anti-inflammatory medicine, resolved. No uric acid-lowering therapy.
- ED discharge paperwork 2013: kidney stone, passed. No procedure.
- No known drug allergies.
- Vaccines: flu yearly through 2018.
No other diagnoses.

documents.title: Outside records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior records. Consistent with what he told me at intake. Problem list confirmed. Nothing to act on.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: request 90-day supplies of metformin 1000 mg BID and atorvastatin 20 mg daily, 3 refills. Pt seen 9/12. Sent per PCP protocol.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Feels well. Work busy, lots of overtime with new contracts. No complaints.
Diabetes: metformin BID, no missed doses he admits to. Saw the optometrist? Not yet, keeps forgetting. Gave him the number again.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 20.
Social: still a few beers on the weekend by his account. Never smoker.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Weight stable from fall. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Feet with intact sensation and pulses. No joint findings.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P: Diabetes well controlled at last check, A1c and CMP today. Lipids today. Continue current meds. Encouraged walking at lunch. Eye exam, again. RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Work question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the warehouse is staying open and they want everyone in. Is diabetes a reason I should be home? Also I'm almost out of the atorvastatin, pharmacy says no refills left.

documents.title: RE: Work question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Darren. Well-controlled diabetes like yours does raise risk a bit but isn't by itself a reason to stop working. Masks, distance on the floor, hand hygiene, and stay home if you have any symptoms. Happy to write something for your employer if you want to request extra precautions. Atorvastatin refill sent, 90 days with refills.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Diabetes check. Doing OK, working long days, eating on the go. Takes metformin with breakfast and dinner. No hypoglycemia (not on anything that would cause it). No foot symptoms. Masks at work all day now.
O: Vitals reviewed, BP fine. Wt about the same. Lungs clear, heart regular. Monofilament intact both feet, pulses good.
A/P: T2DM, stable. A1c, BMP, urine albumin today. Continue metformin and atorvastatin. He finally booked the eye appointment for November. Flu shot next month at a nurse visit, he'll come before shift.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine IM R deltoid, tolerated. Masked, screened at door, no symptoms. Observed briefly, left for work.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Re: Darren Upton, DOB 07/10/1971. Exam date 11/12/2020.
Dilated fundus examination for diabetes. Visual acuity 20/20 OD, 20/25 OS with current glasses. Pupils normal. Intraocular pressures normal. Lens clear. Fundus: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, maculae flat.
Impression: diabetes without retinopathy. Recommend repeat dilated exam in 12 months.
Optometry

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. Pt well, says the past year was "work, work, work." No new symptoms. Has his first COVID vaccine scheduled at a pharmacy next month.
Meds unchanged: metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 20 daily. NKDA.
Alcohol: weekends, social, per pt. No tobacco.
Exam: BP normal. Weight steady around 104 kg. Normal cardiopulmonary exam. Abdomen benign. Feet intact. No tophi. PHQ-2 1 (tired some days, attributes to hours).
Plan: labs today. Colon cancer screening: he is 49, average risk, prefers colonoscopy and getting it over with. Referral placed. Continue meds. Follow up in the fall.

documents.title: COVID-19 vaccines given at a pharmacy
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt sent photo of vaccination card through the portal. Entered two doses Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine, 4/6/2021 and 4/27/2021, given at a retail pharmacy. Lot numbers on card.

documents.title: Screening colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outpatient endoscopy center. Procedure date 08/13/2021.
Indication: average-risk colorectal cancer screening.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: good; mucosa well seen throughout.
Findings: cecum reached and photographed, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve identified. Normal mucosa through the colon. No polyps. Small internal hemorrhoids on retroflexion.
Impression: normal screening colonoscopy.
Recommendation: repeat in 10 years.
Gastroenterology

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine diabetes follow-up. Colonoscopy done in August, normal. Feels fine. Got both COVID shots in the spring.
O: BP 142/92 on arrival, first time above goal here. HR normal. Weight 104. Exam otherwise unremarkable, feet normal.
A/P:
- T2DM: A1c, BMP, urine albumin. Continue metformin.
- Elevated BP reading without a diagnosis. Will repeat at the physical in the spring before calling it anything; he had rushed in from work. Cut back on salty takeout.
- Flu vaccine today.
- Eye exam due, reminder given.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Patient: Darren Upton. Seen 12/02/2021 for annual diabetic eye evaluation.
Dilated exam: no retinopathy in either eye. No macular edema. Optic nerves healthy, cup-to-disc 0.3 OU. Mild presbyopia, new reading add prescribed.
Return 1 year.
Optometry
